subject: SummitForge onboarding — reference architecture sanity & failover tests
messages:
From: Martin Blake <mblake@summitforge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SummitForge integration kickoff: reference design & sandbox window

Hi Olga / Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our call, SummitForge is ready to move into a short partner validation cycle focused on the reference architecture and failover behavior. I've attached the current reference diagram (summitforge-arch-v1.pdf) and a one-page overview.

High-level asks from our side:
- Quick sanity check of the deployment topology (VPC peering + private endpoints)
- Failover tests for regional routing and model fallbacks
- A lightweight baseline perf run with our sample corpus (we can provide JSONL)

We are targeting the sandbox window May 25-26 PT. Can you confirm who on the Redwood side will own each validation area and whether you need any additional account or API access ahead of time?

Thanks,
Martin Blake
Director, Platform Partnerships
SummitForge, Inc.

Attachments: summitforge-arch-v1.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitForge integration kickoff: reference design & sandbox window

Team — looping you in to coordinate the validation slate. Martin shared the reference arch and is asking for a short sanity/pass/failover exercise in their sandbox. Proposed owners below:

- Sergio Alvarez: runtime & perf validation (baseline throughput + latency, warmup behavior, batching profiles)
- Laura Bennett: security & deployment sanity (VPC peering, private endpoints, KMS access, audit logs)
- Aditya Rao: engineering liaison for any minor infra changes and test harnesses (deploy scripts, metrics hooks)

Planned scope (rough):
1) Baseline perf: 1-hour baseline with SummitForge sample corpus to profile p99/p50 and token cost. Deliverable: spreadsheet with charts (sf-failover-testplan.xlsx).
2) Failover & routing: simulate primary region outage and confirm automatic fallback to secondary model variant; validate cache priming and cold-start windows.
3) Security validation: confirm that no PII persists in logs, KMS access path works, and audit logs are emitted to their collector.
4) Runbook verification: validate the shared runbook for a production rollout (shared-runbook.md) and add any SummitForge-specific steps.

Notes / prerequisites: Martin — please send a scoped sample corpus, the sandbox API key, and any network contact to open VPC peering (we should have least-privilege rules). Sergio, please estimate time per test and a minimal infra footprint (GPUs / queue size). Laura, flag any compliance blockers early.

I'll take point on sequencing and documenting results for the partner scorecard.

Olga Petrov
Head, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Martin Blake <mblake@summitforge.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitForge integration kickoff: reference design & sandbox window

Sounds good — I'm penciled for lead on the runtime checks. Preliminary run notes and constraints:

- Baseline perf window: Tue May 25, 09:00–13:00 PT (4h). We'll do incremental traffic ramps: 5%, 25%, 50%, 100% of their expected QPS. Deliverable: sf-failover-testplan.xlsx with graphs + raw metrics.
- Failover/resilience window: Wed May 26, 14:00–18:00 PT. We'll trigger regional failover (simulated AZ/region outage) and measure recovery times and token-loss characteristics.
- Important caveat: SummitForge's topology uses aggressive KV cache sharing across sessions. That means cold-start behavior will dominate the first 30–60 minutes; please set expectations that initial p99s will be higher and that we should measure pre-warm + sustained phases separately.

What I need from SummitForge:
- Sandbox API key with a role allowing us to create a temporary deployment and pull metrics dashboards (read-only where possible).
- A representative sample corpus in JSONL (one prompt per line) and expected QPS numbers so we can size batch windows.
- Confirmation on whether they test with streaming responses or chunked fragmented outputs (affects server push behavior).

Thanks — I'll start drafting the runbook snippets and a minimal infra sizing.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Martin Blake <mblake@summitforge.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SummitForge integration kickoff: reference design & sandbox window

Sergio / Olga — great, thanks for the plan and caveats. We're good with the windows. Quick updates from our side:

- Attached: sample-corpus.jsonl (2.5k lines) and a small harness that can replay traffic.
- Sandbox access: created API key SF-SANDBOX-202705 (scoped) and added sergio@redwood.ai as a user on the sandbox project; you should have invite emails.
- We will test streaming responses (that's how we push partial results to the UI).
- For the KV behavior: the corpus contains a high degree of repeated prefixes — we'll mark a subset as cold-start to help you measure warmup.

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcSFref (arch diagram)
We also uploaded a short checklist to our shared drive; please add any runbook notes to the shared document: https://docs.redwood.ai/handbook/partners/SF-9372

Looking forward to the run — ping me directly if you need network contacts or additional logs.

Martin Blake
Director, Platform Partnerships
SummitForge, Inc.

Attachments: sample-corpus.jsonl (text, 420KB)
